method: COMPILED FROM 3 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Internal Medicine Journal (Royal Australasian College of Physicians; University of Sydney authors) 'Hyperhidrosis: don't sweat it' (published 7 March 2025 (vol 55, issue 10, pp 1626–1631)), 19 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC12515462). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from International Hyperhidrosis Society (sweathelp.org) 'Clinical Guidelines: Primary Focal Axillary Hyperhidrosis' (web page current at retrieval; its treatment algorithm is marked 'Revised February 2025'), 9 claims; LICENCE: Copyright (C) 2026 International Hyperhidrosis Society. All rights reserved. Terms of use: reproduction, retransmission or reprinting is prohibited without prior written permission (read at site footer and https://www.sweathelp.org/sweat-help-home/privacy-policy.html (Terms of Use, COPYRIGHT section)). S3: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from International Hyperhidrosis Society (sweathelp.org) 'Starch Iodine + OnabotulinumtoxinA Injection Protocol for Axillary Treatment' (web page current at retrieval (undated)), 3 claims; LICENCE: Copyright (C) 2026 International Hyperhidrosis Society. All rights reserved. Terms of use: reproduction, retransmission or reprinting is prohibited without prior written permission (read at site footer and https://www.sweathelp.org/sweat-help-home/privacy-policy.html (Terms of Use, COPYRIGHT section)). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 adds S2 and S3, two International Hyperhidrosis Society web pages fetched with curl, scripts, styles and navigation removed, tags stripped and cut to the article text; paraphrased. The S1 claims are unchanged.

claims.claim: **Hyperhidrosis is sweating beyond what thermoregulation needs.** About 5% of US adults are affected (up to 16% in some groups); fewer than half seek care and fewer still are treated well.
claims.locator: Internal Medicine Journal (Royal Australasian College of Physicians; University of Sydney authors), 'Hyperhidrosis: don't sweat it', published 7 March 2025 (vol 55, issue 10, pp 1626–1631), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515462/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Primary hyperhidrosis has no underlying cause.** It is usually focal (axillae first, then palms), starts in adolescence or early adulthood, and runs in families: up to 60% have an affected first-degree relative in palmar cohorts.
claims.locator: Internal Medicine Journal (Royal Australasian College of Physicians; University of Sydney authors), 'Hyperhidrosis: don't sweat it', published 7 March 2025 (vol 55, issue 10, pp 1626–1631), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515462/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Think secondary hyperhidrosis** when sweating is generalised, begins after age 25, or occurs at night; look for an underlying cause.
claims.locator: Internal Medicine Journal (Royal Australasian College of Physicians; University of Sydney authors), 'Hyperhidrosis: don't sweat it', published 7 March 2025 (vol 55, issue 10, pp 1626–1631), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515462/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The burden is real:** around 50% report reduced quality of life, and generalised anxiety, social anxiety and depression occur far more often in people with hyperhidrosis.
claims.locator: Internal Medicine Journal (Royal Australasian College of Physicians; University of Sydney authors), 'Hyperhidrosis: don't sweat it', published 7 March 2025 (vol 55, issue 10, pp 1626–1631), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515462/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Work up the ladder:** topical, oral and device treatments come before injections, ablation or surgery. The four-point Hyperhidrosis Disease Severity Scale can record severity and response.
claims.locator: Internal Medicine Journal (Royal Australasian College of Physicians; University of Sydney authors), 'Hyperhidrosis: don't sweat it', published 7 March 2025 (vol 55, issue 10, pp 1626–1631), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515462/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Topical treatment is first line for focal hyperhidrosis**: easy to use, well tolerated and effective.
claims.locator: Internal Medicine Journal (Royal Australasian College of Physicians; University of Sydney authors), 'Hyperhidrosis: don't sweat it', published 7 March 2025 (vol 55, issue 10, pp 1626–1631), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515462/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Use clinical-strength aluminium chloride (15%–25%), not ordinary 1%–2% antiperspirant.** Response rates reach 98% in the axillae, a little lower on palms and soles.
claims.locator: Internal Medicine Journal (Royal Australasian College of Physicians; University of Sydney authors), 'Hyperhidrosis: don't sweat it', published 7 March 2025 (vol 55, issue 10, pp 1626–1631), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515462/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Apply aluminium salts at bedtime,** when sweating is lowest, daily or every other day; expect benefit in 1–2 weeks.
claims.locator: Internal Medicine Journal (Royal Australasian College of Physicians; University of Sydney authors), 'Hyperhidrosis: don't sweat it', published 7 March 2025 (vol 55, issue 10, pp 1626–1631), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515462/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Irritation is the main problem:** up to 70% get at least mild itch, which eases with continued use. There is no clear evidence tying these antiperspirants to Alzheimer disease or breast cancer.
claims.locator: Internal Medicine Journal (Royal Australasian College of Physicians; University of Sydney authors), 'Hyperhidrosis: don't sweat it', published 7 March 2025 (vol 55, issue 10, pp 1626–1631), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515462/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Topical glycopyrrolate is an alternative** (63% improved in an open-label wipe study). Warn patients to wash their hands afterwards: touching an eye can dilate the pupil.
claims.locator: Internal Medicine Journal (Royal Australasian College of Physicians; University of Sydney authors), 'Hyperhidrosis: don't sweat it', published 7 March 2025 (vol 55, issue 10, pp 1626–1631), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515462/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Oral anticholinergics (glycopyrrolate, oxybutynin) are usually second line for axillary sweating** and first line for generalised sweating. Oxybutynin response was 76% in a systematic review; side effects rise with dose and in older people.
claims.locator: Internal Medicine Journal (Royal Australasian College of Physicians; University of Sydney authors), 'Hyperhidrosis: don't sweat it', published 7 March 2025 (vol 55, issue 10, pp 1626–1631), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515462/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Propranolol suits sweating that flares with stress,** taken regularly or when needed. Take care with bradycardia, low blood pressure, asthma and hypoglycaemia risk.
claims.locator: Internal Medicine Journal (Royal Australasian College of Physicians; University of Sydney authors), 'Hyperhidrosis: don't sweat it', published 7 March 2025 (vol 55, issue 10, pp 1626–1631), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515462/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Botulinum toxin is second or third line,** when topical or device treatment has not worked. It is injected at the dermal-subcutaneous junction.
claims.locator: Internal Medicine Journal (Royal Australasian College of Physicians; University of Sydney authors), 'Hyperhidrosis: don't sweat it', published 7 March 2025 (vol 55, issue 10, pp 1626–1631), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515462/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Axillary injections satisfy up to 96% of patients,** and the effect lasts on average 6–9 months. Mapping the sweating area with a starch-iodine test guides injection.
claims.locator: Internal Medicine Journal (Royal Australasian College of Physicians; University of Sydney authors), 'Hyperhidrosis: don't sweat it', published 7 March 2025 (vol 55, issue 10, pp 1626–1631), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515462/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Compensatory sweating after toxin is uncommon.** Weakness from toxin spreading into muscle is more of a problem in the palms and face than the axillae.
claims.locator: Internal Medicine Journal (Royal Australasian College of Physicians; University of Sydney authors), 'Hyperhidrosis: don't sweat it', published 7 March 2025 (vol 55, issue 10, pp 1626–1631), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515462/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Microwave thermolysis (miraDry) is licensed for axillary hyperhidrosis,** with response up to 90% at 12 months. It needs anaesthesia, reduces underarm hair, and is not for palms or soles.
claims.locator: Internal Medicine Journal (Royal Australasian College of Physicians; University of Sydney authors), 'Hyperhidrosis: don't sweat it', published 7 March 2025 (vol 55, issue 10, pp 1626–1631), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515462/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Endoscopic thoracic sympathectomy is mainly for refractory palmar sweating.** Compensatory sweating elsewhere follows in 80% and can be worse than the original problem, so counsel carefully first.
claims.locator: Internal Medicine Journal (Royal Australasian College of Physicians; University of Sydney authors), 'Hyperhidrosis: don't sweat it', published 7 March 2025 (vol 55, issue 10, pp 1626–1631), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515462/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Try conservative treatment before invasive treatment.** Begin with over-the-counter clinical-strength antiperspirant, then prescription aluminium chloride hexahydrate, the long-standing first line; a 20% solution is the usual prescription.
claims.locator: International Hyperhidrosis Society (sweathelp.org), 'Clinical Guidelines: Primary Focal Axillary Hyperhidrosis', web page current at retrieval; its treatment algorithm is marked 'Revised February 2025', https://www.sweathelp.org/treatments-hcp/clinical-guidelines/primary-focal-hyperhidrosis/primary-focal-axillary.html, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **How to use prescription aluminium chloride:** put it on completely dry skin before bed and wash it off 6 to 8 hours later; washing beforehand is unnecessary and can irritate more. Use it nightly for 1 week until sweating falls, then space applications out to weekly or less while control lasts. Hydrocortisone cream helps irritation.
claims.locator: International Hyperhidrosis Society (sweathelp.org), 'Clinical Guidelines: Primary Focal Axillary Hyperhidrosis', web page current at retrieval; its treatment algorithm is marked 'Revised February 2025', https://www.sweathelp.org/treatments-hcp/clinical-guidelines/primary-focal-hyperhidrosis/primary-focal-axillary.html, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Sweating that comes with known stressful events** (a presentation, a performance) can instead be treated beforehand with an anticholinergic or a short benzodiazepine course.
claims.locator: International Hyperhidrosis Society (sweathelp.org), 'Clinical Guidelines: Primary Focal Axillary Hyperhidrosis', web page current at retrieval; its treatment algorithm is marked 'Revised February 2025', https://www.sweathelp.org/treatments-hcp/clinical-guidelines/primary-focal-hyperhidrosis/primary-focal-axillary.html, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **If antiperspirants fail or cannot be tolerated, onabotulinumtoxinA injection is a next step,** repeated as needed; improvement in the axillae lasts six to eight months on average. If the first result is poor, adjust technique, dose or area and inject again: a second set usually works.
claims.locator: International Hyperhidrosis Society (sweathelp.org), 'Clinical Guidelines: Primary Focal Axillary Hyperhidrosis', web page current at retrieval; its treatment algorithm is marked 'Revised February 2025', https://www.sweathelp.org/treatments-hcp/clinical-guidelines/primary-focal-hyperhidrosis/primary-focal-axillary.html, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Microwave thermolysis (miraDry) destroys sweat glands without surgery,** with results stable to 12 months of follow-up; between one and three sessions may be needed.
claims.locator: International Hyperhidrosis Society (sweathelp.org), 'Clinical Guidelines: Primary Focal Axillary Hyperhidrosis', web page current at retrieval; its treatment algorithm is marked 'Revised February 2025', https://www.sweathelp.org/treatments-hcp/clinical-guidelines/primary-focal-hyperhidrosis/primary-focal-axillary.html, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Topical anticholinergics:** glycopyrronium 2.4% cloths (approved in the US from age 9) cut measured sweat by 50% or more in most users, with dry mouth, redness and stinging the main side effects; sofpironium 12.45% gel is a newer US option.
claims.locator: International Hyperhidrosis Society (sweathelp.org), 'Clinical Guidelines: Primary Focal Axillary Hyperhidrosis', web page current at retrieval; its treatment algorithm is marked 'Revised February 2025', https://www.sweathelp.org/treatments-hcp/clinical-guidelines/primary-focal-hyperhidrosis/primary-focal-axillary.html, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Oral options** are anticholinergics (glycopyrrolate, oxybutynin, propantheline), propranolol, clonidine and diltiazem. Warn about dry mouth, blurred vision, urinary retention, fast heart rate and constipation, and take particular care with children, athletes and outdoor workers, who can overheat.
claims.locator: International Hyperhidrosis Society (sweathelp.org), 'Clinical Guidelines: Primary Focal Axillary Hyperhidrosis', web page current at retrieval; its treatment algorithm is marked 'Revised February 2025', https://www.sweathelp.org/treatments-hcp/clinical-guidelines/primary-focal-hyperhidrosis/primary-focal-axillary.html, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Local surgery** (curettage, liposuction, laser, alone or combined) is another option; **complete excision of underarm tissue is no longer advised** because the scarring can restrict shoulder movement.
claims.locator: International Hyperhidrosis Society (sweathelp.org), 'Clinical Guidelines: Primary Focal Axillary Hyperhidrosis', web page current at retrieval; its treatment algorithm is marked 'Revised February 2025', https://www.sweathelp.org/treatments-hcp/clinical-guidelines/primary-focal-hyperhidrosis/primary-focal-axillary.html, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Sympathectomy (ETS) only for carefully selected patients once everything else has failed:** it works for palmar sweating but less well for the axillae, and patients must understand the limited benefit and the risk of compensatory sweating.
claims.locator: International Hyperhidrosis Society (sweathelp.org), 'Clinical Guidelines: Primary Focal Axillary Hyperhidrosis', web page current at retrieval; its treatment algorithm is marked 'Revised February 2025', https://www.sweathelp.org/treatments-hcp/clinical-guidelines/primary-focal-hyperhidrosis/primary-focal-axillary.html, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Map the sweating area first with Minor's starch-iodine test:** paint the dry axilla with iodine, let it dry, dust lightly with cornstarch, wait 10 to 15 minutes for the blue-purple change and outline it.
claims.locator: International Hyperhidrosis Society (sweathelp.org), 'Starch Iodine + OnabotulinumtoxinA Injection Protocol for Axillary Treatment', web page current at retrieval (undated), https://www.sweathelp.org/education-and-resources/starch-iodine-onabotulinumtoxina-injection-protocol-for-axillary-treatment.html, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Dose: onabotulinumtoxinA 50 units per axilla.** Reconstitute each 100-unit vial with 4 mL of preservative-free 0.9% saline and inject intradermally into twelve to 15 sites about 1.5 cm apart, staggered, dividing the 50 units evenly and raising a small wheal at each.
claims.locator: International Hyperhidrosis Society (sweathelp.org), 'Starch Iodine + OnabotulinumtoxinA Injection Protocol for Axillary Treatment', web page current at retrieval (undated), https://www.sweathelp.org/education-and-resources/starch-iodine-onabotulinumtoxina-injection-protocol-for-axillary-treatment.html, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Expect an effect in about a week and relief for about 7 months** (up to 12 months in a quarter). Re-treat when sweating returns. If sweating persists after 2 weeks, re-map with starch-iodine and top up the missed areas with about 2–5 units per site.
claims.locator: International Hyperhidrosis Society (sweathelp.org), 'Starch Iodine + OnabotulinumtoxinA Injection Protocol for Axillary Treatment', web page current at retrieval (undated), https://www.sweathelp.org/education-and-resources/starch-iodine-onabotulinumtoxina-injection-protocol-for-axillary-treatment.html, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Refer patients who fail an initial trial of topicals for specialist care** (usually a neurologist or dermatologist); advanced therapies control sweating in nearly everyone.
claims.locator: Internal Medicine Journal (Royal Australasian College of Physicians; University of Sydney authors), 'Hyperhidrosis: don't sweat it', published 7 March 2025 (vol 55, issue 10, pp 1626–1631), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515462/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **In Australia, botulinum toxin is subsidised by Medicare and the PBS for axillary hyperhidrosis only.** Palmar, plantar and facial toxin, iontophoresis devices, ablation and surgery mostly mean out-of-pocket costs.
claims.locator: Internal Medicine Journal (Royal Australasian College of Physicians; University of Sydney authors), 'Hyperhidrosis: don't sweat it', published 7 March 2025 (vol 55, issue 10, pp 1626–1631), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12515462/, retrieved 2026-09-23
